title.narrative: Design and Establishment of a Programme Monitoring and Evaluation Information Management System

description.narrative: CAFOD East Africa's approach to Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) is to track Impacts and Outcomes using high level indicators across all CAFOD supported programmes and projects through a framework for collecting and analysing information which is fed back into the project design and implementation. In order to effectively assess the Impacts and Outcomes at programme and project levels, baselines, mid-term and end of project evaluations are always conducted with gender and age disaggregated data, across all indicators as defined in the CAFOD logframes. Impact studies are conducted in which intended, and unintended impact on individual families are tracked over time; changes within the family, within the communities and within the external social, political, and economic context are analysed. Comparisons are made between each of the different CAFOD supported project locations, particularly to assess commonalities between families and districts to determine success factors for increased resilience. A number of key sources exist to obtain information on various CGF and Institutional supported projects and programmes at CAFOD level: Webpromise, partner submitted progressive reports, partner evaluation reports, need assessment reports, reports manager etc. There is therefore potentially a plethora of information being collected by all CAFOD partners at all levels for all kinds of projects and programmes. CAFOD EA will therefore engage an individual consultant to design a simple yet functional, efficient and effective Programme M&E Information Management System that will help in monitoring programme progress against high level Impact, Outcome and Output indicators, and assist CAFOD programme staff to generate, access and monitor programme information efficiently and to the benefit of the programme's high level programme goals and outcomes. This system will be implemented for all CAFOD supported projects to track performance indicators set out in the log frames, and to critically analyse progress towards agreed milestones throughout the life of each project. Progress monitoring against output milestones will either be reported quarterly or bi-annually reflecting gender analysis, age group and location disaggregated data. This quantitative progress reporting will be supported by qualitative assessments of wider indirect impacts of project outputs on HHs and communities through evaluations.
